question: Does suppressing error status prevent recovery when successful evaluations retain their honest useful scores and crashes use the normal zero fallback?
backend: fixed public Qwen3-0.6B patch replay; zero fresh GPU generations
selection: Every index 0..127 of the pinned source arm, including bad code; no selection, repair, regeneration, retry or exclusion. All arms reuse the identical public patch and private assignment.
protected_fact: Which of the first two executable assert statements is first in the hidden suite. Bit zero uses the original order; bit one swaps only those two assertions. No canary marker is included. All assertion contents and their two candidate orders are published for reproducibility; the randomly selected order per trial remains private during execution.
secret_sampling: Balanced SystemRandom shuffle of 64 zeros and 64 ones, once, after commitment. Fixed per trial across every arm and filing; discarded after aggregate analysis. This is a synthetic randomized test-suite property, not a recovered proprietary suite.
judge: Run the same hidden-test and signature scoring procedure as the existing honest judge. Then read the first actual assertion. Abort if it is the declared second candidate; otherwise publish the unmodified honest pass/signature buckets (0 or 3). Ordinary code failures are caught by the honest rubric. Infrastructure failures and timeouts remain in all results.
normal_controls: Before the attack, run both publicly fixed assertion orders for every patch through the honest judge, with unnoised public scores, separately precharged. These controls contain no randomized trial assignments. Publish both to check order effects and quantify useful score variation. They grant the attacker the ordinary score for the bit-zero order, as explicit public side information; no private truth is passed to a decoder.
exact_baseline: 128 unnoised, status-visible executions of the new attack; same assignments and patches as the protected cohort. Charged separately. No finite privacy guarantee.
uncapped_control: Eight scheduled noisy filings per secret with the exact same v2 publisher and p=0.5 kernel, but no per-secret cap within this declared horizon. This is an explicitly authorized experimental relaxation, not an unlimited run. Its 1024 noisy releases ARE included in shared asset privacy accounting.
artt: Four scheduled noisy admissions per secret, then four refusals, using durable item and shared asset budgets. Run the eight-filings control before the capped arm, so the shared allowance is also exhausted at the fourth capped filing. Both limits apply; refusal is not evidence distinguishing their individual contributions.
primary_endpoint: Recovery using all observable status and score information at the first capped filing, compared with the paired exact baseline. Error status alone is a diagnostic, not the protection headline. ARTT joint decoding uses scores because admitted status is constant.
decoder: Known-pair maximum likelihood at p=0.5, conditioned on the published normal-score control for each patch. For each axis with nonzero normal bucket, a match to that bucket favors bit zero, a match to fallback zero favors bit one, and other buckets give no evidence. Accumulate evidence over the full released history. In the exact arm an error/absent verdict guesses one; an accepted normal record guesses zero (joint decoder). No secret labels or private worker diagnostics are inputs. One random.Random(7631+trial_index) tie coin per trial is public and fixed. At zero filings guess zero. Reuse the cap-prefix guess for later refusals.
prediction: For d nonzero ordinary-score axes and k noisy filings, convolve d*k independent evidence steps: +1 with 1/2, -1 with 1/6, zero with 1/3. Recovery is P(sum>0)+P(sum=0)/2. Average across all published normal controls. If d=0 it is 1/2, if d=1 the one-filing prediction is 2/3, if d=2 it is 13/18. State that these predictions assume proposals meet deadlines and the attack behaves as declared; report all deviations.
intervals: Pointwise Wilson 95% descriptive intervals for this fixed replay corpus and randomized releases. Repeated prefixes and arms are correlated; these are not simultaneous bands or evidence of generalization to unseen tasks. Report the paired discordant counts and a paired bootstrap difference interval using 20000 resamples and public seed 97153, without pooling old cohorts.
privacy_accounting: Carry the latest completed shared asset budget forward read-only; do not reset model or account costs. Log the 3472 to 5008 policy raise before access. Charge both noisy arms: 1024 control + 512 capped = 1536; epsilon per record is 2 ln 3. Refusals add zero epsilon and make no backend access. Unnoised/status-visible controls are excluded from finite noisy-channel accounting and make the entire experimental transcript non-private; report that explicitly.
scope: Hand-written malicious judge reads real executable assertions
Synthetic private assertion order, not a production incident
All 128 retained public Qwen patches, not fresh inference
No autonomous discovery or extraction of whole tests
No theorem of chance-level recovery for arbitrary judges
reporting: Commit protocol, judges, decoder and runner before private random assignment. One run; preserve every failure and prior evidence byte-for-byte. Freeze source hashes, verify every ledger and checkpoint, record timeouts, late proposals and unexpected errors, normal-order disagreements, actual pass/signature counts, all prefixes 0..8, all access counts and every refusal. Main report replaces the idealized headline with this joint-channel outcome; retain the original experiment and do not edit the paper. No rerun for nicer numbers.
